node-1.label: Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis for 1 month

node-2.label: Medical history includes elevated white blood cell count and inguinal lymphadenopathy discovered 9 years prior; 4 years after initial presentation, fatigue, weight loss, and loss of appetite occurred

node-3.label: Current illness began 1 month prior to admission with asymptomatic 'green-yellow welts' and swelling of the glans penis; swelling became progressively painful and evolved to the size of an 'orange' over 4 days

node-4.label: Previous treatments with topical antibiotics, antifungal agents, hydrogen peroxide soaks, warm compresses, and cephalexin showed no improvement

node-5.label: Physical examination: patient appeared healthy; glans penis and corona grossly edematous, with a 3.7 × 3.3-cm tender, firm ulcer on the ventral surface of the penis with overlying black eschar, adherent yellow crust, and granulation tissue; no urethral discharge

why.why: Both the pathologist and radiologist independently confirm that the biopsy findings (atypical CD20+/CD79a+/CD5+ clonal B lymphocytes) and PET-CT findings (FDG-avid abdominal and peripancreatic lymph nodes) establish a malignant B-cell lymphoma with secondary penile ulceration. This further validates the penile malignancy/neoplastic ulcer hypothesis and raises confidence from 0.95 to 0.97.

The expert analyses explicitly exclude an infectious/necrotizing process: the biopsy demonstrates a clonal B-cell lymphoproliferative neoplasm, and the lack of response to antimicrobial therapy is consistent with a non-infectious cause. Confidence is lowered from 0.02 to 0.01.

The pathologist and radiologist both state that the biopsy and imaging findings exclude inflammatory/autoimmune causes. The gold-standard biopsy evidence of malignant B-cell lymphoma makes an inflammatory/autoimmune ulcerative disorder extremely unlikely, reducing confidence from 0.03 to 0.01.

node-9.label: Penile ulcer biopsy shows dermal infiltrate of atypical CD20+/CD79a+/CD5+ B lymphocytes with clonal IgH rearrangement

node-10.label: PET-CT reveals FDG-avid abdominal and peripancreatic lymph nodes

node-11.label: Patient has systemic B-cell lymphoma, likely mantle cell lymphoma, with secondary penile involvement

why.why: Both expert analyses affirm a systemic malignant B-cell lymphoma, most likely mantle cell lymphoma, with secondary penile involvement. The PET-CT showing FDG-avid abdominal and peripancreatic nodes supports systemic disease, while the CD5+ clonal B-cell immunophenotype supports mantle cell lymphoma. Because cyclin D1/FISH testing is unavailable, confidence is raised from 0.85 to 0.90 rather than higher.

node-12.label: Penile ulceration from secondary involvement by systemic mantle cell lymphoma (CD5+ B-cell lymphoma)

why.why: The pathologist and radiologist both reaffirm that the biopsy (CD20+/CD79a+/CD5+ clonal B cells with IgH rearrangement) and PET-CT (FDG-avid abdominal/peripancreatic nodes) establish systemic B-cell lymphoma with secondary penile involvement, and CD5+ is most consistent with mantle cell lymphoma. However, both experts emphasize that cyclin D1, t(11;14)/CCND1 FISH, and SOX11 are unavailable, so definitive MCL subtyping is not possible. Therefore MCL remains the most likely subtype but is not confirmed, keeping confidence at 0.85.

node-13.label: Penile ulceration from secondary involvement by systemic CLL/SLL (CD5+, CD23+ B-cell lymphoma)

attrs.why: A CD5+ clonal B-cell phenotype (node-9) is also compatible with CLL/SLL, so this is the next fine-grained subcategory of the generic frontier node-6. The belief notes that cyclin D1/FISH and CD23 data are unavailable, which is exactly why this alternative CD5+ subtype cannot be excluded from the malignancy hypothesis.

node-14.label: Primary penile/cutaneous B-cell lymphoma (no systemic disease)

attrs.why: As a finer subdivision of frontier node-6, a primary cutaneous/penile B-cell lymphoma could produce the ulceration supported by node-9. However, node-10 (FDG-avid abdominal and peripancreatic nodes) supports systemic disease, so this refinement is assigned low confidence relative to the systemic hypothesis in the belief.

node-15.label: Penile ulceration due to a non-lymphoid penile malignancy (e.g., squamous cell carcinoma)

attrs.why: The generic frontier node-6 also encompasses non-lymphoid tumors, so a carcinoma or melanoma of the penis is a logically finer subtype. Nevertheless, the clonal CD20+/CD79a+/CD5+ B-cell infiltrate of node-9 and the absence of epithelial malignancy findings argue strongly against this refinement, consistent with the belief's exclusion of non-B-cell etiologies.

node-16.label: Cyclin D1, t(11;14)/CCND1 FISH, and SOX11 test results are not yet available
